status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1), approved 2025-07-04, added section 168(n) to the tax code through its section 70307, allowing a 100 percent depreciation deduction for qualified production property: the portion of nonresidential real property used as an integral part of manufacturing, production or refining, with construction beginning after 2025-01-19 and before 2029-01-01 and placed in service in the United States or a territory after 2025-07-04 and before 2031-01-01. IRS Notice 2026-16 gives interim guidance and invited comments by 2026-04-20; it sets no China-specific or relocation condition. Separately, the pharmaceutical tariff proclamation published 2026-04-09 sets a lower 20 percent rate for companies with approved onshoring plans, but it is a tariff measure covering all source countries.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1) was approved; its section 70307 adds a 100 percent depreciation allowance for qualified production property placed in service in the United States.
Proclamation 11020 was published, setting a 20 percent pharmaceutical duty rate (rising to 100 percent in 2030) for companies with approved onshoring plans.

title: Give tax and financial incentives to companies onshoring production from China
uncertainties: Public Law 119-21 was confirmed on GovInfo by number, bill and date; section 70307 and the property rules were read in the IRS notice, which quotes the statute, not in the law's own text, which is very long. The notice prints no issuance date, so it is not placed on the timeline. The permanent 100 percent bonus depreciation provision is described in a law-firm summary only. No program tied to moving production from China was found in three searches. The tax incentive is general to domestic production rather than targeted at relocation from China; it is treated as a partial match because companies moving production from China qualify, though a reader could treat it as a parallel program.
